faq.q: What does the scale on a map mean?
faq.a: The scale tells you how much real distance one unit on the map stands for. A scale of 1 to 100,000 means 1 cm on the map is 100,000 cm on the ground, which is 1 km.
asks: What does 1:100,000 mean on a map?

faq.a: A small-scale map shows a big area, like a continent, with little detail. Things on it look small, so a whole city may be just a dot.
asks: Is a world map large or small scale?

faq.a: A large-scale map shows a small area, like a town or a school, with lots of detail. Buildings and paths look large on it.
asks: Which map shows the most detail?

faq.q: How do I work out real distance from a map?
faq.a: Measure the distance on the map with a ruler, then use the scale. On a 1 to 100,000 map, every centimetre is 1 km, so 3 cm means 3 km on the ground.
asks: How do I use a scale bar?

faq.q: Why can't a world map show my street?
faq.a: On a world map 1 cm stands for hundreds or thousands of kilometres, so your whole town would be smaller than a dot. You need a large-scale street map to see it.
asks: Why do maps leave things out?

facts: A scale of 1:100,000 means 1 cm on the map equals 1 km on the ground.
Ordnance Survey Explorer walking maps of Britain use a scale of 1:25,000, so 4 cm on the map is 1 km.

quiz.say: On a map with a scale of 1 to 100,000, two villages are 5 centimetres apart. How far apart are they really?
quiz.show: Scale 1:100,000. Villages 5 cm apart on the map are really…
quiz.why: At this scale 1 cm stands for 1 km, so 5 cm stands for 5 km.

wrong.1: 50 km would need each centimetre to stand for 10 km.
wrong.2: 500 m would need each centimetre to stand for 100 m.

quiz.say: Which map is large scale, showing the most detail?
quiz.why: A school plan shows a small area in great detail, so it is large scale.

wrong.1: A map of Asia covers a huge area with little detail, so it is small scale.
wrong.2: A world map is the smallest scale of all.
